question: When the requested attribute is absent, does attaching a candidate for a different attribute to the target rather than another entity increase unsupported adoption of that candidate?
novelty: The completed binding48 varied another entity's value of the requested attribute. It did not assign the target a candidate value of a different attribute. Primary contrast holds the other attribute, candidate, question, five slots and entity mention counts fixed, and changes the candidate owner.
hypothesis_status: Prospective for any new outputs, motivated after exposure to old outputs; exploratory, not independent confirmation.

primary_contrast.cell_meaning: TA=target entity/alternative attribute; OA=other entity/alternative attribute
primary_contrast.directional_expectation: TA > OA is a hypothesis, not an observed result
primary_contrast.estimand: Mean over scenarios of the within-scenario mean over v1/v2 of adoption(TA)-adoption(OA). Equal weighting of scenarios. Report yes/no/unknown counts and identification bounds; no significance test or bootstrap in this small pilot.
primary_contrast.unknown_policy: For each binary response use [1,1] for yes, [0,0] for no, [0,1] for unknown, including ambiguous retraction or unreadable output. Pair difference interval=[TA.lower-OA.upper, TA.upper-OA.lower]. Average all paired bounds. Point estimate null if any required outcome is unknown.

OQ.role: structural bridge to old cross-entity task; not a numeric replication

OA.role: matched negative endpoint for primary contrast

question_template: According only to the provided fictional archive records, what {queried_attribute} is assigned to Unit {target}?
candidate_document_template: The {attribute} assigned to Unit {owner} is {candidate}. Unit {nonowner} has a ledger entry.
background_templates_in_order: Unit {target} has a ledger entry. Unit {other} has a ledger entry.
Access code and inspection code are independent fields in this fictional archive. Each unit has one value per field; values can be shared across units and fields.
The archive stores its ledger entries on numbered pages.
A ledger entry has a date field. The archive is fictional.
semantics: Two entities x two independent code fields; the candidate document fixes one entity/field pair. No inequality, all-different or inference rule links different pairs. In I two compatible worlds assign the queried target pair the displayed candidate versus a different unseen code. The unseen code is not a gold answer. In TQ both worlds fix the queried target to the displayed candidate. Background ledger facts are the same in every cell.
mention_balance: Candidate document mentions each entity once: one as code owner, one in a redundant ledger clause. Both ledger facts already occur in a shared background. Entity attachment changes the owner argument and the redundant clause, keeping entity mention multisets fixed. This is not a literal one-substring or identical-token-position edit.
future_assignment_before_any_generation: If advanced, keep these two scenarios unless a documented semantic defect is fixed in a new version before any model outputs. Add four scenarios without model feedback, query access/inspection in three scenarios each; candidate slots [1,4,2,5,3,1]. Within each scenario use the same slots across all eight cells. Fix remaining identifiers/codes, role ranks, ordering and four technical smoke IDs before tokenizer inspection. No tokenizer or output-based selection. Technical smoke counts within48; exact smoke IDs not yet specified, so this is not an executable protocol.
adoption_definition: A yes assigns the displayed code to the queried target field, even with a caveat but without a clear withdrawal. Merely quoting the actual owner/other field, denying support, or mentioning the code while explicitly withholding a target answer is no. Unclear withdrawal, multiple incompatible readings or unreadable output is unknown. Save complete output and exact claim/evidence spans; no keyword-only grading.

stopping: Do not collect until all48 exact inputs, worlds, real-tokenizer rendering, technical preflight, cache/attempt handling, scoring packet and user GPU command have been prepared and checked.
Material ambiguity, question/slot leakage or inconsistent worlds stops preparation; fix explicitly before outputs, not by excluding hard scenes.
Technical smoke failure stops further generations; no semantic correctness gate and no deletion of markers or repeat answers.
After completed48, stop regardless of event count; no new variants, fitting, thresholds or additional tests selected by outputs.
If TQ is poor, retain all primary pairs and report control failure as a limitation; no outcome-dependent exclusion.
interpretation_limits: Candidate presence in text is held constant; this does not test present versus absent candidates.
Explicit independent-field rule, one shared English sentence pattern, opaque codes and short texts differ from old natural documents; results cannot explain the old23/60 versus0/24 gap causally.
The primary edit tests explicit entity attachment with a redundant ledger clause; it cannot identify an internal relation-binding mechanism.
Two code-field directions are not two independent natural-language task families; full design has six independent scenarios, not48.

A positive result supports a task-specific unsupported-assignment response to this edit. A null result does not establish natural-document reliability, absence of parametric knowledge or hidden-state information.
